title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost by shipping automated sensible defaults and UI tooling for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profile recommendations. This PR implements: 1) autopick defaults for per-route batching and cache TTL based on historical request size/latency distributions; 2) quantization profile registry and heuristics to recommend quantization levels by model family/workload; 3) a unit-economics dashboard endpoint and CLI helper to show expected $/k-token under current defaults; 4) rollout plan for safe canary (10% traffic) + automatic fallback on QoS regressions. Checklist: [x] server-side heuristics implemented; [x] quant profile registry + migration; [x] unit-econ tooling + API; [x] console UI changes + docs; [x] end-to-end tests + perf benchmarks; [x] staged rollout config. Related: Linear ENG-1023 (autotune defaults), ENG-1108 (unit-econ dashboard), SUP-2145 (customer request for aggressive defaults). Design summary: heuristics compute a target batch size and cache TTL per route using 7d sliding window of traffic, constrained by latency SLO and GPU memory headroom; quant profiles are stored per model with compatibility tags (fp16, int8, q4_0) and a conservative score that factors accuracy runs from the eval harness. The unit-econ tool synthesizes observed latency and token counts with instance pricing to estimate $/k-token and recommends savings from batching/quant. Rollout: default off for enterprise customers, on for hosted with safe canary at 10%, automatic rollback on 3%+ QoS degradation over 5m. Testing: microbenchmarks (latency, throughput), integration tests (routing, fallbacks), canary on perf-canary cluster. Migration notes: added DB table quant_profiles; includes a migration with backfill that marks profiles as "recommended" for known redwood-verified models. See docs link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/autotune (internal).

review_comments: Ethan Wu: strong work on the heuristics. Two asks: (1) can we bound memory use on large-batch scenarios? (2) add a short-circuit to avoid batching for sub-50 token requests to keep p99 low.
Aisha Patel: answered: added a soft memory headroom check and route-level override; default min_batch_size=8 to avoid hurting tiny requests.
Sofia Martin: unit-econ numbers look plausible but we should tag the estimation with price-timestamp so customers can reproduce; also request more tests around quant accuracy degradation.
Aisha Patel: added price-timestamp to API response and added automated eval jobs for top-3 models per family to capture delta accuracy on q4_0/int8 profiles.
Liam O'Connor: approve after CI fixes; please ensure migration backfill is non-blocking for large deployments.
Aisha Patel: migration runs as background job and includes chunked commits; updated migration docs in PR.
ci_checks: CI / unit-tests: initial run failed (race in heuristics_test) -> fixed and rerun -> pass
CI / perf/regression: no regression observed on perf-canary cluster
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and caching; introduces quantization profile registry and conservative recommendations; exposes a unit-economics estimation API and console panel to help teams understand $/k-token impact of batching and quantization; safe canary rollout and automatic fallback on QoS regressions.
notes_for_release: Default enabled for hosted customers behind 10% canary. Enterprise customers remain opt-in by default. Recommend communications to affected customers and link to ops playbook.
testing_and_qa: Microbenchmarks and e2e tests included; perf-canary observed ~18% median token-cost reduction for long-tail chat workloads with q4_0 + batching; p99 latency impact within SLO for tested routes. QA: run rw unit-econ estimate on staging and validate numbers against perf-canary metrics.
manual_deployment_steps: 1) apply DB migration; 2) deploy backend and console; 3) enable canary flag in perf-canary config; 4) monitor autotune.metrics.unit_econ and autotune.events.rollback; 5) promote to 100% after 48h with no QoS regression.
customer_impact_summary: Expected reduction in token-unit cost for chat-heavy routes when recommendations are accepted; conservative defaults minimize QoS regression risk. Enterprise customers are opt-in; support ticket SUP-2145 tracked a customer request for more aggressive defaults.
